headline: Chinese robot maker JAKA is launching a heavy-duty wheeled humanoid robot, the Kargo50, for moving bins around factories, and a robot arm that can handle 50 kilograms, the Zu50, at a Shanghai industry fair.
score_reason: Pool 4 kept: the launch is on 12 Oct 2026 and the article matches the headline; the Kargo50 has no published specifications.
importance_line: A Chinese maker is moving its wheeled humanoid robots from lighter tasks to heavier factory hauling, which matters to factory workers and managers weighing more automation, but the Kargo50 has no published payload or specifications yet, and the results quoted for the earlier Kargo10 are the company's own.
source: Pandaily, citing Shanghai Securities News and Jiemian News
summary: Pandaily, a news site covering Chinese technology, reports, citing Shanghai Securities News, that JAKA Robotics, a Chinese maker of collaborative robots (arms built to work alongside people), is using the 26th China International Industry Fair in Shanghai, which opens on 12 Oct 2026, to launch two machines it calls global debuts: the Kargo50, a heavy-duty wheeled humanoid for moving totes (storage bins) and other materials between stations on a factory floor, and the Zu50, an arm listed on JAKA's website as handling up to 50 kg. JAKA has not yet published specifications for the Kargo50; it points instead to its smaller Kargo10, which the company says cut its time per tote from 105 to 28 seconds at customer factories, and Jiemian News saw two of its wheeled humanoids at the booth carry an engine and tighten its screws as a pair.
notes: Read in full: the fulltext fetch was empty, so the text was taken from the Pandaily page itself (HTTP 200). machine_action is true because Pandaily reports, from Jiemian News, two wheeled humanoids carrying and screwing at the booth workcell (a trade-fair demonstration seen the day before the fair) and the Kargo10 in commercial use; the Kargo50 itself has no reported demonstration.
